data.title: Security Appliances Identifiable From Outside the Perimeter
data.summary:
The organisation's perimeter security products — mail gateway, web application firewall,
VPN concentrator and remote access portals — are identifiable from outside through banners,
headers, certificates and published scan data.
data.description:
Knowing which products defend a perimeter lets an adversary select techniques that are
known to pass them and avoid those that will not. Mail gateway identification in particular
shapes phishing: the attachment types, link handling and sandbox behaviour of each product
are well documented.

Remote access portals are the more serious exposure. They are internet-facing by necessity,
their versions are frequently disclosed in responses, and they have been among the most
heavily exploited products in recent years, so version disclosure translates directly into
targeting.

Public scan databases mean this information is available without the organisation ever
observing a scan.
data.recommendation:
* Suppress version detail in banners, headers and error pages for all perimeter products.
* Review the organisation's own entries in public scan databases to see what is disclosed.
* Prioritise patching of remote access products on the assumption that their presence and
  version are already known.
* Use certificates that do not disclose internal naming or product identity.
data.short_recommendation: Suppress version detail at the perimeter and audit public scan data.
